detail: Last raced 1991. Vic Lee cut from two two-car teams (Labatt's + Listerine) to one team, M Team Shell with Listerine (Harvey, Bellm, Soper).
Securicor sponsorship moved from Vic Lee BMW to the Rouse Toyota team; Rouse ran 3 Carinas (Hoy, Rouse, Thyrring/Bailey) after 2 in 1991.
Last raced 1991 (Andy Middlehurst, Sierra RS Cosworth). Middlehurst moved to Nissan Janspeed for 1992. Absent from 1992 entry list.
Last raced 1991 (Gravett, Sierra Sapphire). Gravett joined the works Peugeot Talbot Sport team for 1992; Trakstar did not run the Peugeot (built in-house by Peugeot UK).
Last raced 1991 (Frank Sytner M3). Absent from 1992 entry list.
Last raced 1991 (Lindgren, Andersson). Peggen Andersson came back alone in 1993 as Peggen Motorsport (M3, rounds 1-2), a separate small entry.
Last raced 1991 (Mark Hales Lancer then Galant). No Mitsubishi in 1992.
No Mitsubishi entered from 1992 on.
Last raced 1991 (Flux/Neal/Musetti M3). Absent from 1992 entry list.
Last raced 1991 (MacKay, Lyall 318is). Lyall drove for Techspeed in 1992. Not to be confused with Roger Dowson's 'RD Motorsport' Mazda team.
Last raced 1991 (Belmont: Jeff Wilson/Tony Bardy). Absent from 1992 entry list.
Last raced 1991 (Dave Brodie Sierra 4x4 rounds 10-13). Absent from 1992 entry list.
Semi-works Cavaliers (David Leslie, Verdon-Roe then Portman), Cavaliers bought from Dave Cook and re-engineered by RML. 2 cars.
Works 405 Mi16 for Robb Gravett, Ian Flux 2nd car at final round. A privateer 405 (ACE Motorsport) had already raced in 1991.
Peugeot works entry starts (privateer ACE 405 had 2 starts in 1991).
Patrick Watts, Mazda 323F, Shell/Clarion/Yokohama backing. 1 car.
Mazda arrives with the 323F.
Independent Carina for James Kaye; became the Park Lane Toyota Junior Team in 1993 (2 cars).
Matt Neal BMW M3 then 318is. Became Team Dynamics for 1993.

Last raced 1992. Vic Lee Motorsport liquidated after owner Vic Lee was jailed for drug trafficking; assets bought by the new Team Dynamics. Vic Lee Racing came back only in 2000 in the new Class B (Peugeot 306).
Last raced 1992. BMW GB withdrew after rule changes; Prodrive lost the BMW deal (took Subaru rally work). A planned Prodrive/AMG Mercedes C-Class never raced.

Works BMW moves from Prodrive (BMW GB) to Schnitzer (BMW Motorsport, after it left the DTM). Soper + Winkelhock; Winkelhock champion. Motor Sport Jan 1993 issue: BMW 'almost certainly' back via Schnitzer.
Works Toyota passes from Andy Rouse to TOM's GB (Norfolk). New Carina E. Rouse last ran Toyota in 1992.
Works Ford Mondeo (Rouse, Radisich), debut at round 7/8 (Pembrey) after the season had started. 2 cars.
New manufacturer: Renault 19 16v for Tim Harvey and Alain Menu. Confirmed as a 1993 works entry in Motor Sport Jan 1993 issue. Operating company not confirmed in sources read.
Renault arrives.
Rimstock Racing merged with Euroracing staff and bought Vic Lee assets; renamed Team Dynamics. 2-3 BMW 318is (Neal, Bellm, Portman).
Last raced 1992 (Dennis Leech Sierra RS Cosworth rounds 7 and 9-12).
Last raced 1992 (Sean Walker, Karl Jones, M3). Absent from 1993 entry list (Wikipedia only for 1993 list).
Last raced 1992 as Ian Forrest Racing (M3, rounds 8 and 12). Absent 1993 (Wikipedia only for 1993 list).
Grows to 2 works cars (Gravett, O'Brien) plus Ian Flux in a third 405 run by Roy Kennedy Racing.
3 Primeras (O'Dor, Percy, Needell) after 2 in 1992.
Works Vauxhall passes from Dave Cook Racing (last season 1993) to RML; Ecurie Ecosse name ends, RML now runs the works Cleland/Allam cars. Dave Cook Racing left the paddock.
Volvo return first reported October 1993; 850 estate shown January 1994, confirmed at Geneva March 1994; debut Thruxton 4 April 1994. Lammers + Rydell. 3-year TWR deal.
Volvo arrives.
Italian works team, 155 TS for Tarquini and Simoni; Tarquini champion. Announcement date not found.
Alfa Romeo arrives.
Back to 2 cars (Watts from Mazda, O'Brien); Gravett left.
2 Xedos 6 (Leslie, Neal); Neal's car written off at Silverstone, Mazda withdrew mid-season before Knockhill (Wikipedia only for withdrawal timing).
Last raced 1994 (withdrew mid-season). Team Magic Mazda 323F entered in 1995 but never raced.
No Mazda raced from 1995.
Last raced 1994. Motor Sport March 1995 preview lists Nissan as gone.
No Nissan in 1995 (back in 1996 with Rouse).
Renault UK and Williams GP Engineering deal of 8 September 1994; WTCE runs the Laguna from 1995 (Menu, Hoy). Renault manufacturers' champion 1995.
Alfa Corse returned to Italy; Prodrive runs the works 155s (Warwick, Simoni, Tarquini). Prodrive back in BTCC after 1993-94 gap.
Schnitzer left after 1994 (Motor Sport March 1995); BMW team for Cecotto and Brabham. Exact running team unclear (Wikipedia: BMW UK arm; Motor Sport: 'BMW Motorsport International Team').
Doubtful: Wikipedia names Toyota Motorsport GmbH; Motor Sport March 1995 names TTE; Motor Sport Dec 1995 calls TOM's GB the builders. Mobil 1 sponsor.
New manufacturer: Accord for David Leslie and James Kaye, exclusive Yokohama deal.
Honda arrives.
Team Dynamics switches from BMW to an independent Ford Mondeo (Matt Neal); wins the 1995 independents cup.
Last raced 1995. Toyota GB withdrew support (Motor Sport Dec 1995). Team Brookes ran an ex-works Carina privately in 1996.
Last raced 1995. Alfa withdrew at end of 1995 (Wikipedia only).
No Alfa from 1996 (Nordauto 156 announced for 1998 never raced; Class B 156 in 2000).

operator: Audi Sport UK (Richard Lloyd / David Ingram)
detail: A4 quattro, Biela confirmed by Dec 1995 (Motor Sport); Biela champion, Bintcliffe 2nd car.
Audi arrives.
Works Ford moves from Andy Rouse to WSR with Reynard-built cars (WSR favourite in Dec 1995). Radisich + Robertson.
After losing Ford, Rouse runs semi-works Nissan Primeras (Ayles, McAuley), one car later in the year.
Nissan back after one year away.
Schnitzer returns as BMW works team (Winkelhock, Ravaglia, Kox 3rd car late).
Lee Brookes, ex-works 1995 TOM's Carina; won the independents cup. Peugeot 406 in 1997, Hondas later.
Last raced 1996: BMW's last works BTCC season. Only BMW in 1997 is Colin Gallie's 1994 318i (Team DCRS).
Triple Eight founded late 1996 by Derek Warwick, Roland Dane and Ian Harrison; takes the works Vauxhall from RML.
RML leaves Vauxhall and runs a full works Nissan Primera team (Leslie, Reid); Rouse out.
Last raced 1996. Andy Rouse team gone from 1997.
Prodrive takes over Honda from MSD (Thompson, Tarquini).
MSD leaves Honda and runs works Peugeot 406 (Harvey, Watts). 1992-96 Peugeot was run in-house by Peugeot UK.
Dave Cook back with a single 1994 BMW 318i for Colin Gallie; DC Cook Motorsport ran Renault (Rustad) and Honda (Paula Cook) 1998-99. Link between DCRS and DC Cook Motorsport assumed, not confirmed.
Return with 156 (Larini, Giovanardi) announced for late 1998 rounds, never raced (Wikipedia only).
No BMW entries in 1998 (TRM 320i entered in 1999 never raced) (Wikipedia only).
Last raced 1998. Peugeot did not enter 1999 (costs, lack of pace); works return 2001.
No Peugeot in 1999 or 2000 main class.
Last raced 1998 (fwd A4). Withdrawal date not found (Wikipedia + 1990sbtcc).
No Audi from 1999.
Ford two-year deal with Prodrive, replacing WSR from 1999 (Reid, Menu).
Straight swap: WSR takes Honda from Prodrive (Thompson, Kox).
Last raced 1999. Renault UK announced withdrawal 14 July 1999 when WTCE contract ended.
No Renault in 2000 (Arena International ran a private Laguna in 1999 only).
Last raced 1999. Volvo announced it would leave when the TWR contract ended; month from Radermecker interview (told in August 1999).
No Volvo in 2000.
Last raced 1999. Nissan Motor (GB) press release 28 Sept 1999. Nissan make stays via privateers (Team Dynamics, PRO Motorsport, Bintcliffe Sport).
3 cars: third Accord (Tarquini) prepared by JAS Motorsport; WSR still lead operator (Wikipedia only).

detail: Class B only (Peugeot 306 GTi): Vic Lee Racing back in the BTCC paddock.
DC Cook Motorsport withdrew after Snetterton 1999 (budget); last raced 1999.
Last raced 1993 as works Vauxhall operator (Cleland, Allam). Contract went to RML; announcement date not found.
No Toyota in 1997: Team Brookes switched to Peugeot (Kimber-Smith ran one 2000 round in an old Carina).
